economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month earnings available to common over market capitalization (E/P).
sign_rationale: A low price relative to earnings signals a value premium from risk or overextrapolated pessimism.
reference: Basu 1977 (Journal of Finance); Fama and French 1992 (Journal of Finance); Jaffe Keim and Westerfield 1989 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Loss firms leave the ranked domain and are carried as a separate indicator (Fama-French 1992 E(+)/P); across all firms the relation is U-shaped (Jaffe Keim and Westerfield 1989).

economic_definition: Latest common book equity over market capitalization (B/M).
sign_rationale: High book value relative to market value earns the value premium.
reference: Rosenberg Reid and Lanstein 1985 (Journal of Portfolio Management); Fama and French 1992 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Negative common equity gives a negative ratio; Fama-French drop non-positive book equity.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month free cash flow over market capitalization.
sign_rationale: Cash generated per dollar of price is a cash-flow-to-price value ratio that is harder to manage than earnings.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Hou Karolyi and Kho 2011 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Negative free cash flow leaves the ranked domain and is carried as a separate indicator.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month common dividends over market capitalization (D/P).
sign_rationale: Among dividend payers a higher yield is a price-scaled value ratio that earns higher average returns.
reference: Litzenberger and Ramaswamy 1979 (Journal of Financial Economics); Naranjo Nimalendran and Ryngaert 1998 (Journal of Finance); Keim 1985 (Journal of Financial Economics); Christie 1990 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: U-shaped: zero payers earn high returns (Keim 1985; Christie 1990) so non-payers leave the ranked domain and the sign is tested among payers; dividends are read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero so a non-payer that never tags a dividend has no value.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month research and development expense over market capitalization.
sign_rationale: Markets underprice expensed intangible investment so high R&D relative to market value earns higher returns.
reference: Chan Lakonishok and Sougiannis 2001 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month gross profit over enterprise value.
sign_rationale: An enterprise-value yield on gross profit combines the enterprise-multiple value effect with gross profitability.
reference: Loughran and Wellman 2011 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis); Novy-Marx 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Enterprise value is non-positive for net-cash firms and then flips the yield sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing preferred stock and minority interest read as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating cash flow over enterprise value.
sign_rationale: A capital-structure-neutral cash-flow yield carries the cash-flow-to-price value effect.
reference: Loughran and Wellman 2011 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis); Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Enterprise value is non-positive for net-cash firms and then flips the yield sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing preferred stock and minority interest read as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating income over enterprise value.
sign_rationale: The inverse enterprise multiple is a capital-structure-neutral value ratio.
reference: Loughran and Wellman 2011 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis)
admission_note: Enterprise value is non-positive for net-cash firms and then flips the yield sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing preferred stock and minority interest read as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month revenue over enterprise value.
sign_rationale: Sales relative to firm value is a value ratio that stays defined for loss-making firms.
reference: Barbee Mukherji and Raines 1996 (Financial Analysts Journal); Loughran and Wellman 2011 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis)
admission_note: Enterprise value is non-positive for net-cash firms and then flips the yield sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing preferred stock and minority interest read as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month revenue over market capitalization (S/P); the monotone inverse of ps_ttm.
sign_rationale: Cheap sales relative to price predict higher returns and stay defined through losses.
reference: Barbee Mukherji and Raines 1996 (Financial Analysts Journal); Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating cash flow over market capitalization (C/P); the monotone inverse of pcf_ttm.
sign_rationale: Cash flow to price is a classic value ratio in the contrarian-extrapolation evidence.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Negative operating cash flow leaves the ranked domain and is carried as a separate indicator.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month EBITDA over enterprise value; the monotone inverse of ev_ebitda (the enterprise multiple).
sign_rationale: Firms with low enterprise multiples earn higher returns.
reference: Loughran and Wellman 2011 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis)
admission_note: Enterprise value is non-positive for net-cash firms and then flips the yield sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing preferred stock and minority interest read as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month gross profit over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: High margins reflect pricing power and profitable firms earn higher returns.
reference: Novy-Marx 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics); Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating income over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: Operating profitability predicts higher returns.
reference: Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month net income over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: Bottom-line profitability predicts higher returns.
reference: Haugen and Baker 1996 (Journal of Financial Economics); Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month EBITDA over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: Pre-depreciation operating profitability predicts higher returns.
reference: Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Single-quarter gross profit over single-quarter revenue.
sign_rationale: The most recent quarter's margin carries the profitability premium with less staleness than a trailing sum.
reference: Novy-Marx 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality.

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating income over single-quarter revenue.
sign_rationale: The most recent quarter's operating profitability carries the profitability premium.
reference: Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality.

economic_definition: Single-quarter net income over single-quarter revenue.
sign_rationale: The most recent quarter's net profitability carries the profitability premium.
reference: Haugen and Baker 1996 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month net income over average total assets.
sign_rationale: More profitable firms earn higher returns (profitability premium).
reference: Haugen and Baker 1996 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month net income to common over average common equity.
sign_rationale: High return on equity predicts higher returns (q-factor ROE).
reference: Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies); Haugen and Baker 1996 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Negative average common equity inverts the ratio so a loss can read as a positive return.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month NOPAT over average invested capital net of cash.
sign_rationale: High returns on operating capital signal durable profitability independent of leverage.
reference: Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Invested capital net of cash can be non-positive for cash-rich firms and then flips the sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing minority interest reads as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month NOPAT over average invested capital net of cash and goodwill.
sign_rationale: Returns on organic operating capital strip acquisition premia from the profitability signal.
reference: Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Invested capital net of cash and goodwill can be non-positive and then flips the sign; its debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and missing minority interest and goodwill read as zero.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month gross profit over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Gross profits-to-assets is the cleanest accounting measure of economic profitability and predicts higher returns.
reference: Novy-Marx 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating income over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Operating profitability scaled by assets predicts higher returns.
reference: Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Trailing operating income plus depreciation less working-capital accrual changes over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Cash-based operating profitability predicts returns and subsumes the accrual anomaly.
reference: Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2016 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev add R&D back to operating profit and this construction does not; an issuer that has never tagged a mapped inventory alias has zero inventory change.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating cash flow over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Operating cash profitability predicts higher returns.
reference: Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2016 (Journal of Financial Economics); Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research)

economic_definition: Nine binary signals of profitability and its change and of liquidity and leverage and issuance and efficiency (0 to 9).
sign_rationale: Financially strong firms outperform weak ones especially among value stocks.
reference: Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: The equity-offering signal compares period-end share counts a year apart and is comparable only where daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase both counts and labeled incomparable otherwise (piotroski_f_cash_issuance reads issuance from cash proceeds instead); long-term debt missing beside reported short-term debt is absent within the reported total and is zero for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias while a switch to an unmapped alias leaves the leverage signal and so the score without a value.

economic_definition: Nine binary Piotroski signals (0 to 9) with the no-equity-issuance signal read from trailing cash proceeds of equity issuance.
sign_rationale: Financially strong firms outperform weak ones; cash-flow issuance keeps the score free of share-count splits.
reference: Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Equity issuance is read from cash proceeds (option exercises included) only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and is never imputed as none since an absent discrete quarter cannot prove absence from a year-to-date or annual fact (non-issuers that never tag the concept have no score); long-term debt missing beside reported short-term debt is absent within the reported total and is zero for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias while a switch to an unmapped alias leaves the leverage signal and so the score without a value.

economic_definition: Altman Z-score with book equity in the equity-to-liabilities term.
sign_rationale: A higher Z means lower bankruptcy risk and distressed firms earn anomalously low returns.
reference: Altman 1968 (Journal of Finance); Dichev 1998 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Altman Z-score with market equity in the equity-to-liabilities term.
sign_rationale: A higher Z means lower bankruptcy risk and high-distress firms earn anomalously low returns.
reference: Dichev 1998 (Journal of Finance); Altman 1968 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Beneish eight-variable earnings-manipulation M-score.
sign_rationale: A higher probability of earnings manipulation predicts lower returns.
reference: Beneish 1999 (Financial Analysts Journal); Beneish Lee and Nichols 2013 (Financial Analysts Journal)

economic_definition: Ohlson O-score bankruptcy index (no GNP deflator).
sign_rationale: Higher bankruptcy probability predicts lower returns (distress anomaly).
reference: Ohlson 1980 (Journal of Accounting Research); Dichev 1998 (Journal of Finance); Griffin and Lemmon 2002 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month income tax expense over trailing net income.
sign_rationale: Taxable income high relative to book income signals conservative persistent earnings and predicts higher returns.
reference: Lev and Nissim 2004 (The Accounting Review)
admission_note: Negative net income inverts the ratio.

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month revenue.
sign_rationale: The one-year sign is contested: multi-year sales growth is overextrapolated and predicts low returns (Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994) while recent revenue news drifts in its own direction (Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006); pre-registered two-sided.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Mixed one-year evidence: the trailing growth rate averages four seasonal quarterly growth rates whose freshest component is the positively signed revenue_q_growth_yoy.

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing revenue with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Multi-year sales growth is overextrapolated and mean-reverts so glamour firms underperform.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month gross profit.
sign_rationale: Profit growth is fundamental momentum that markets underreact to.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984); Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month operating income.
sign_rationale: Earnings growth is fundamental momentum that markets underreact to.
reference: Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance); Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month net income over the absolute prior base.
sign_rationale: Earnings growth is fundamental momentum that markets underreact to.
reference: Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance); Foster Olsen and Shevlin 1984 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month diluted EPS over the absolute prior base.
sign_rationale: Earnings-per-share growth is the unscaled numerator of standardized unexpected earnings and drifts.
reference: Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research); Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Trailing diluted EPS sums four quarters each filed on its own split basis and is comparable only where the quarters share one filing clock or daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase them and labeled incomparable otherwise.

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month operating cash flow.
sign_rationale: Cash-flow growth is fundamental momentum that markets underreact to.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month free cash flow.
sign_rationale: Free-cash-flow growth is fundamental momentum that markets underreact to.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month income tax expense.
sign_rationale: Rising tax expense signals rising taxable earnings that markets underreact to (tax expense momentum).
reference: Thomas and Zhang 2011 (Journal of Accounting Research)

economic_definition: Quarter-over-quarter growth of trailing twelve-month revenue.
sign_rationale: Sequential improvement in trailing sales is recent fundamental news that markets underreact to.
reference: Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: A one-quarter change of a trailing sum compares overlapping 365-day spans; the engine labels every value incomparable.

economic_definition: Quarter-over-quarter growth of trailing twelve-month diluted EPS.
sign_rationale: Sequential improvement in trailing EPS is recent earnings news that markets underreact to.
reference: Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: A one-quarter change of trailing EPS compares overlapping 365-day spans so the engine labels every value incomparable (its split basis would also be gated per row).

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing diluted EPS with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Long-horizon earnings growth does not persist but is extrapolated into prices so high past growth underperforms.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Per-share trailing EPS twelve quarters apart is comparable only where daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase both ends to one split basis and labeled incomparable otherwise.

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing operating cash flow with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Long-horizon cash-flow growth mean-reverts but is extrapolated into prices.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing gross profit with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Long-horizon profit growth mean-reverts but is extrapolated into prices.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing operating income with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Long-horizon profit growth mean-reverts but is extrapolated into prices.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing EBITDA with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Long-horizon profit growth mean-reverts but is extrapolated into prices.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of trailing free cash flow with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Long-horizon cash-flow growth mean-reverts but is extrapolated into prices.
reference: Lakonishok Shleifer and Vishny 1994 (Journal of Finance); Chan Karceski and Lakonishok 2003 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in trailing gross margin in fraction points.
sign_rationale: Gross-margin improvement is a fundamental signal of future earnings that prices underreact to.
reference: Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review); Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in trailing operating margin in fraction points.
sign_rationale: Operating-margin improvement signals future earnings that prices underreact to.
reference: Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review); Akbas Jiang and Koch 2017 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in trailing net margin in fraction points.
sign_rationale: Profit-margin improvement signals future earnings that prices underreact to.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in operating income over average assets.
sign_rationale: A rising profitability trend predicts higher returns.
reference: Akbas Jiang and Koch 2017 (The Accounting Review); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in trailing return on average common equity.
sign_rationale: Rising ROE signals higher expected investment returns (q5 expected growth; dRoe anomaly).
reference: Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies); Hou Mo Xue and Zhang 2021 (Review of Finance)

economic_definition: Single-quarter gross margin less the same fiscal quarter's margin a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonally differenced gross-margin improvement is fresh fundamental news that prices underreact to.
reference: Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating margin less the same fiscal quarter's margin a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonally differenced operating-margin improvement is fresh fundamental news.
reference: Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review); Akbas Jiang and Koch 2017 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Single-quarter net margin less the same fiscal quarter's margin a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonally differenced net-margin improvement is fresh fundamental news.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Single-quarter revenue growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonal-random-walk revenue surprises predict drift in the same direction.
reference: Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: Single-quarter gross-profit growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonally differenced profit growth is fresh fundamental news that prices underreact to.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984); Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating-income growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonal-random-walk earnings surprises drift (post-earnings-announcement drift).
reference: Foster Olsen and Shevlin 1984 (The Accounting Review); Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: Single-quarter net-income growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonal-random-walk earnings surprises drift (post-earnings-announcement drift).
reference: Foster Olsen and Shevlin 1984 (The Accounting Review); Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: Single-quarter diluted-EPS growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: The seasonal EPS change is the numerator of standardized unexpected earnings and drifts.
reference: Foster Olsen and Shevlin 1984 (The Accounting Review); Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Per-share quarters a year apart are comparable on one filing's restated comparative or daily-bar split epochs (R1d) and labeled incomparable otherwise; filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release.

economic_definition: Single-quarter basic-EPS growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: The seasonal EPS change is the numerator of standardized unexpected earnings and drifts.
reference: Foster Olsen and Shevlin 1984 (The Accounting Review); Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Per-share quarters a year apart are comparable on one filing's restated comparative or daily-bar split epochs (R1d) and labeled incomparable otherwise; filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release.

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating-cash-flow growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonally differenced cash-flow growth is fresh fundamental news that prices underreact to.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)

economic_definition: Single-quarter free-cash-flow growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Seasonally differenced free-cash-flow growth is fresh fundamental news that prices underreact to.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)

economic_definition: Single-quarter revenue growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential sales improvement is the most recent fundamental news.
reference: Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Single-quarter gross-profit growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential profit improvement is the most recent fundamental news.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating-income growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential earnings improvement is the most recent fundamental news.
reference: Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Single-quarter net-income growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential earnings improvement is the most recent fundamental news.
reference: Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating-cash-flow growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential cash-flow improvement is the most recent fundamental news.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Single-quarter free-cash-flow growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential free-cash-flow improvement is the most recent fundamental news.
reference: Novy-Marx 2015 (NBER Working Paper 20984)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Single-quarter diluted-EPS growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential EPS improvement is the most recent earnings news.
reference: Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Adjacent quarters come from different filings so the per-share pair is comparable only where daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase it and labeled incomparable otherwise; sequential quarters also carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths.

economic_definition: Single-quarter basic-EPS growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Sequential EPS improvement is the most recent earnings news.
reference: Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Adjacent quarters come from different filings so the per-share pair is comparable only where daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase it and labeled incomparable otherwise; sequential quarters also carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths.

economic_definition: This quarter's seasonal diluted-EPS growth less the previous quarter's seasonal growth.
sign_rationale: Earnings acceleration is underreacted news beyond the level of earnings growth.
reference: He and Narayanamoorthy 2020 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Built from per-share seasonal growth: comparable only where each EPS pair shares a filing clock or daily-bar split epochs (R1d) and labeled incomparable otherwise; filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release.

economic_definition: This quarter's seasonal revenue growth less the previous quarter's seasonal growth.
sign_rationale: Revenue acceleration is underreacted news in the spirit of earnings acceleration.
reference: He and Narayanamoorthy 2020 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: This quarter's seasonal gross-margin change less the previous quarter's seasonal change.
sign_rationale: Accelerating margin improvement is underreacted fundamental news.
reference: He and Narayanamoorthy 2020 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: This quarter's seasonal operating-margin change less the previous quarter's seasonal change.
sign_rationale: Accelerating margin improvement is underreacted fundamental news.
reference: He and Narayanamoorthy 2020 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of total assets.
sign_rationale: Firms that grow assets fastest earn low subsequent returns (investment effect).
reference: Cooper Gulen and Schill 2008 (Journal of Finance); Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of total assets with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Sustained asset expansion predicts low returns (investment effect).
reference: Cooper Gulen and Schill 2008 (Journal of Finance); Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of common book equity.
sign_rationale: Equity-financed balance-sheet expansion behaves like investment and predicts lower returns.
reference: Cooper Gulen and Schill 2008 (Journal of Finance); Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Three-year compound annual growth of common equity with positive endpoints required.
sign_rationale: Sustained equity expansion behaves like investment and predicts lower returns.
reference: Cooper Gulen and Schill 2008 (Journal of Finance); Fama and French 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in net operating assets over lagged total assets.
sign_rationale: Growth in net operating assets is investment and accrual build-up that predicts lower returns.
reference: Hirshleifer Hou Teoh and Zhang 2004 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Net operating assets net out debt; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month capital expenditure.
sign_rationale: Capital-investment growth predicts lower returns as growth options convert to assets in place.
reference: Anderson and Garcia-Feijoo 2006 (Journal of Finance); Xing 2008 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Single-quarter capital-expenditure growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Capital-investment growth predicts lower returns.
reference: Anderson and Garcia-Feijoo 2006 (Journal of Finance); Xing 2008 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Single-quarter capital-expenditure growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Capital-investment growth predicts lower returns.
reference: Anderson and Garcia-Feijoo 2006 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Trailing capital expenditure over trailing depreciation and amortization.
sign_rationale: Investment well above replacement signals empire building or overinvestment that predicts lower returns.
reference: Titman Wei and Xie 2004 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis)

economic_definition: Trailing capital expenditure over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: High capital investment relative to sales predicts lower returns.
reference: Titman Wei and Xie 2004 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis)

economic_definition: Trailing research and development expense over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: Expensed intangible investment is underpriced; the published sales-scaled evidence is weaker than the market-scaled one.
reference: Chan Lakonishok and Sougiannis 2001 (Journal of Finance); Lev and Sougiannis 1996 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of trailing twelve-month research and development expense.
sign_rationale: Markets underreact to the benefits of R&D increases.
reference: Eberhart Maxwell and Siddique 2004 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Single-quarter R&D expense growth over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier.
sign_rationale: Markets underreact to the benefits of R&D increases.
reference: Eberhart Maxwell and Siddique 2004 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Single-quarter R&D expense growth over the immediately preceding fiscal quarter.
sign_rationale: Markets underreact to the benefits of R&D increases.
reference: Eberhart Maxwell and Siddique 2004 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Sequential quarters carry fiscal seasonality and unequal quarter lengths; quarterly origin only when adjacency is proven.

economic_definition: Trailing net income less operating cash flow over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Accrual-heavy earnings are less persistent than cash earnings and investors overweight them.
reference: Sloan 1996 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Trailing net income less operating cash flow over absolute trailing net income.
sign_rationale: Accruals scaled by earnings identify firms whose earnings are mostly accruals and predict lower returns.
reference: Hafzalla Lundholm and Van Winkle 2011 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in operating working capital over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Working-capital accruals mean-revert and predict lower returns.
reference: Sloan 1996 (The Accounting Review)
admission_note: Short-term debt missing beside reported long-term debt is absent within the reported total (an intermittent revolver or current portion keeps the value) and is zero for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias; otherwise missing short-term debt has no value rather than a spurious accrual.

economic_definition: Change in net operating assets less debt (total assets less cash and short-term investments less total liabilities) over average total assets (broad accruals: the change in book equity less the change in cash and short-term investments).
sign_rationale: Less reliable accruals are less persistent and predict lower returns.
reference: Richardson Sloan Soliman and Tuna 2005 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Debt cancels (net operating assets less debt equals total assets less cash and short-term investments less total liabilities) so no debt concept is read; Richardson Sloan Soliman and Tuna net short-term investments against financial assets separately and keep preferred stock and minority interest outside common equity while here they sit in the residual.

economic_definition: Net operating assets over lagged total assets (cumulative accruals).
sign_rationale: Balance-sheet bloat from cumulative accruals predicts lower returns.
reference: Hirshleifer Hou Teoh and Zhang 2004 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Net operating assets net out debt; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Interest-bearing debt over stockholders equity (book leverage).
sign_rationale: Low-leverage firms earn higher returns (leverage puzzle).
reference: George and Hwang 2010 (Journal of Financial Economics); Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Negative stockholders equity inverts the ratio so the most levered firms read as unlevered; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Interest-bearing debt over total assets.
sign_rationale: Low-leverage firms earn higher returns (leverage puzzle).
reference: George and Hwang 2010 (Journal of Financial Economics); Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Long-term debt over total assets.
sign_rationale: Low-leverage firms earn higher returns (leverage puzzle).
reference: George and Hwang 2010 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Long-term debt missing beside reported short-term debt is absent within the reported total and is zero for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias; otherwise (a switch to an unmapped alias) missing long-term debt has no value.

economic_definition: Debt net of cash over trailing EBITDA.
sign_rationale: Heavier debt service burdens proxy for distress and low-leverage firms earn higher returns.
reference: George and Hwang 2010 (Journal of Financial Economics); Campbell Hilscher and Szilagyi 2008 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Non-positive trailing EBITDA inverts the ratio; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Trailing operating income over absolute trailing interest expense.
sign_rationale: Better debt-service capacity means lower distress risk and distressed firms earn low returns.
reference: Campbell Hilscher and Szilagyi 2008 (Journal of Finance); Dichev 1998 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Current assets over current liabilities.
sign_rationale: Liquidity strength lowers distress risk and is a Piotroski strength signal.
reference: Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research); Campbell Hilscher and Szilagyi 2008 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Current assets less inventory over current liabilities.
sign_rationale: Liquidity strength lowers distress risk.
reference: Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research); Campbell Hilscher and Szilagyi 2008 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Inventory is zero only for an issuer that reports total assets and has never tagged a mapped inventory alias; a switch to an unmapped alias or a skipped quarter has no value rather than the current ratio.

economic_definition: Cash and short-term investments over current liabilities.
sign_rationale: Cash holdings are positively related to expected returns and lower distress risk.
reference: Palazzo 2012 (Journal of Financial Economics); Campbell Hilscher and Szilagyi 2008 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Interest-bearing debt over market capitalization (market leverage).
sign_rationale: Market leverage is largely the value effect (the A/ME and A/BE effects are equal and opposite and sum to B/M in Fama and French 1992) and net financial leverage is negatively priced after operating B/P (Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007); pre-registered two-sided.
reference: Bhandari 1988 (Journal of Finance); Fama and French 1992 (Journal of Finance); Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Mixed evidence and largely subsumed by B/M: report it controlled for book_to_market; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Total assets over market capitalization (A/ME market leverage).
sign_rationale: A/ME is B/M times A/BE: its positive premium in Fama and French 1992 is the value effect net of an equal and opposite book-leverage effect and net financial leverage is negatively priced after operating B/P (Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007); pre-registered two-sided.
reference: Fama and French 1992 (Journal of Finance); Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Mixed evidence and largely subsumed by B/M: report it controlled for book_to_market.

economic_definition: Trailing equity issued less repurchased over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Firms issue equity when overvalued and repurchase when undervalued so net issuers underperform.
reference: Pontiff and Woodgate 2008 (Journal of Finance); Bradshaw Richardson and Sloan 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Issuance and repurchases are read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero since an absent discrete quarter cannot prove absence from a year-to-date or annual fact; firms that never repurchase or never issue have no value so the heavy-issuer short leg is thinned.

economic_definition: Trailing long-term debt issued less repaid over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Net debt financing predicts lower returns (external financing anomaly).
reference: Bradshaw Richardson and Sloan 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Spiess and Affleck-Graves 1999 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Debt issuance and repayment are read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero; firms without one of the flows have no value.

economic_definition: Net equity plus net debt financing over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Total net external financing predicts lower returns.
reference: Bradshaw Richardson and Sloan 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Each financing flow is read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero; firms missing any flow (often non-repurchasers) have no value.

economic_definition: Year-over-year growth of period-end shares outstanding.
sign_rationale: Net share issuance predicts lower returns.
reference: Pontiff and Woodgate 2008 (Journal of Finance); Daniel and Titman 2006 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Period-end share counts are balances that no filing restates for a split and are comparable only where daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase both counts to one split basis and labeled incomparable otherwise.

economic_definition: Trailing common dividends over trailing earnings available to common.
sign_rationale: A high payout signals management confidence in earnings persistence.
reference: Arnott and Asness 2003 (Financial Analysts Journal)
admission_note: Negative earnings invert the ratio; dividends are read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero so non-payers that never tag a dividend have no value.

economic_definition: Trailing repurchases less issuance over market capitalization.
sign_rationale: Net repurchase yield predicts higher returns.
reference: Boudoukh Michaely Richardson and Roberts 2007 (Journal of Finance); Ikenberry Lakonishok and Vermaelen 1995 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Repurchases and issuance are read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero; firms without one of the flows have no value.

economic_definition: Trailing dividends plus repurchases less issuance over market capitalization.
sign_rationale: Net payout yield predicts returns better than dividend yield.
reference: Boudoukh Michaely Richardson and Roberts 2007 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Dividends repurchases and issuance are each read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero so buyback-only and dividend-only firms that never tag the other flow have no value.

economic_definition: Trailing gross dividends plus gross repurchases over market capitalization.
sign_rationale: Total payout yield predicts higher returns.
reference: Boudoukh Michaely Richardson and Roberts 2007 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Dividends and repurchases are each read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero so buyback-only and dividend-only firms that never tag the other flow have no value.

economic_definition: Trailing net payout plus net debt paydown over market capitalization.
sign_rationale: Cash returned to all capital providers extends the net payout yield effect.
reference: Boudoukh Michaely Richardson and Roberts 2007 (Journal of Finance); Bradshaw Richardson and Sloan 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Each payout and debt flow is read only when tagged in every quarter of the trailing year (the fiscal-year bucket falls back to the annual value) and never imputed as zero; firms missing any flow have no value.

economic_definition: Trailing revenue over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Efficient asset use predicts higher future profitability and returns.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in revenue over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Rising asset turnover predicts higher future earnings that prices underreact to.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Days sales outstanding: average receivables times 365 over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: A longer collection period lengthens the cash conversion cycle which predicts lower returns.
reference: Wang 2019 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Days inventory outstanding: average inventory times 365 over trailing cost of revenue.
sign_rationale: Inventory build-up lengthens the cash conversion cycle and predicts lower returns.
reference: Wang 2019 (Journal of Financial Economics); Thomas and Zhang 2002 (Review of Accounting Studies)

economic_definition: Days payables outstanding: average payables times 365 over trailing cost of revenue.
sign_rationale: Longer supplier financing shortens the cash conversion cycle.
reference: Wang 2019 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: DSO plus DIO less DPO in days.
sign_rationale: Firms with long cash conversion cycles earn lower returns.
reference: Wang 2019 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Twelve-quarter standard deviation of year-over-year trailing diluted-EPS growth.
sign_rationale: Volatile earnings are less persistent and firms with volatile fundamentals earn lower returns.
reference: Huang 2009 (Journal of Empirical Finance); Dichev and Tang 2009 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Its elements are trailing-twelve-month growth rates whose 365-day spans never pass the stdev_q single-quarter chain proof so every value is labeled incomparable.

economic_definition: Price times point-in-time shares outstanding.
sign_rationale: Small firms earn higher average returns (size effect).
reference: Banz 1981 (Journal of Financial Economics); Fama and French 1992 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Twenty-day average daily dollar trading volume.
sign_rationale: Thinly traded stocks earn a liquidity premium; dollar volume also proxies size.
reference: Brennan Chordia and Subrahmanyam 1998 (Journal of Financial Economics); Amihud 2002 (Journal of Financial Markets)

economic_definition: Mean absolute daily return per dollar traded (x 1e9) over the positive-volume days of the last 21 XNYS sessions.
sign_rationale: Illiquid stocks earn a premium for their price impact.
reference: Amihud 2002 (Journal of Financial Markets)
admission_note: A line with fewer than 19 positive-volume days or observed returns in the window has no value (zero_volume_in_window or window_gaps) so the most thinly traded names of the illiquid tail are missing.

economic_definition: Mean daily share volume over the last 21 XNYS sessions divided by the verified DEI shares outstanding.
sign_rationale: High-turnover stocks earn lower returns: a liquidity premium on low turnover.
reference: Datar Naik and Radcliffe 1998 (Journal of Financial Markets)
admission_note: Only lines with a verified DEI share count have a value: multi-class and ADR and unlinked lines and withheld counts are missing and a window holding an exact split or stock-dividend ratio (R1d classifier) has no value.

economic_definition: Total return from 252 to 21 trading days before formation (skips the latest month).
sign_rationale: Past winners keep outperforming past losers over 3 to 12 months.
reference: Jegadeesh and Titman 1993 (Journal of Finance); Carhart 1997 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Total return over the last 252 trading days.
sign_rationale: Twelve-month winners keep outperforming; the latest month adds a reversal component.
reference: Jegadeesh and Titman 1993 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Total return over the last 126 trading days.
sign_rationale: Six-month winners keep outperforming six-month losers.
reference: Jegadeesh and Titman 1993 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Total return over the last 63 trading days.
sign_rationale: Short-formation momentum is positive but weaker than six to twelve months.
reference: Jegadeesh and Titman 1993 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Adjusted close over its highest adjusted close in the last 252 XNYS sessions minus one.
sign_rationale: Stocks near their 52-week high keep outperforming because investors anchor on the high.
reference: George and Hwang 2004 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Total return over the last 21 trading days.
sign_rationale: Last month's winners reverse next month (short-term reversal from liquidity provision).
reference: Jegadeesh 1990 (Journal of Finance); Lehmann 1990 (Quarterly Journal of Economics)

economic_definition: Annualized 60-day realized volatility of daily log returns.
sign_rationale: High-volatility stocks earn anomalously low returns.
reference: Ang Hodrick Xing and Zhang 2006 (Journal of Finance); Baker Bradley and Wurgler 2011 (Financial Analysts Journal)

economic_definition: Annualized 252-day realized volatility of daily log returns.
sign_rationale: High-volatility stocks earn anomalously low returns (low-volatility anomaly).
reference: Baker Bradley and Wurgler 2011 (Financial Analysts Journal); Ang Hodrick Xing and Zhang 2006 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Largest daily return over the last 21 XNYS sessions.
sign_rationale: Lottery-like stocks with extreme positive daily returns are overpriced and earn low future returns.
reference: Bali Cakici and Whitelaw 2011 (Journal of Financial Economics)

economic_definition: Annualized zero-target semideviation (root mean square of the negative daily returns) over the last 60 XNYS sessions.
sign_rationale: Semideviation is downside volatility: low-volatility evidence implies lower returns while downside-risk evidence implies a premium.
reference: Ang Chen and Xing 2006 (Review of Financial Studies); Ang Hodrick Xing and Zhang 2006 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Published evidence disagrees on the sign: Ang Chen and Xing price downside beta positively while the low-volatility literature prices total volatility negatively; tested two-sided.

economic_definition: Single-quarter net income over common equity at the prior quarter end (q-factor ROE).
sign_rationale: High current profitability signals high expected investment returns and predicts higher returns.
reference: Hou Xue and Zhang 2015 (Review of Financial Studies); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality; the value is labeled quarterly only when the opening balance is proven to be the prior quarter end; the numerator is net income including discontinued and extraordinary items where Hou Xue and Zhang use income before extraordinary items.

economic_definition: Single-quarter net income over total assets at the prior quarter end.
sign_rationale: Firms with high current profitability earn higher returns and quarterly ROA is its timely form.
reference: Balakrishnan Bartov and Faurel 2010 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality; the value is labeled quarterly only when the opening balance is proven to be the prior quarter end; the numerator is net income including discontinued and extraordinary items where the published constructions use income before extraordinary items.

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating income over net operating assets at the prior quarter end.
sign_rationale: Core operating profitability on net operating assets predicts higher returns.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality; the value is labeled quarterly only when the opening balance is proven to be the prior quarter end; net operating assets net out debt which is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value).

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month operating income over net operating assets at the start of the trailing year.
sign_rationale: Core operating profitability on net operating assets predicts higher returns.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Net operating assets net out debt; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Single-quarter gross profit over total assets at the prior quarter end.
sign_rationale: Gross profits-to-assets is the cleanest accounting measure of economic profitability and predicts higher returns.
reference: Novy-Marx 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality; the value is labeled quarterly only when the opening balance is proven to be the prior quarter end.

economic_definition: Single-quarter gross profit less SG&A (before R&D; selling plus general and administrative expense when no SG&A total is tagged) over total assets at the prior quarter end.
sign_rationale: Operating profitability before R&D predicts higher returns and subsumes gross profitability.
reference: Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2015 (Journal of Financial Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality; the value is labeled quarterly only when the opening balance is proven to be the prior quarter end.

economic_definition: Single-quarter operating cash flow over total assets at the prior quarter end.
sign_rationale: Cash profitability predicts higher returns and is less exposed to accrual reversal than earnings.
reference: Ball Gerakos Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2016 (Journal of Financial Economics); Sloan 1996 (The Accounting Review)
admission_note: A single-quarter level carries fiscal seasonality; the value is labeled quarterly only when the opening balance is proven to be the prior quarter end.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month free cash flow over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Cash flow after investment is the quality-minus-junk cash profitability measure and predicts higher returns.
reference: Asness Frazzini and Pedersen 2019 (Review of Accounting Studies)

economic_definition: Seasonal change in quarterly net income over the sample standard deviation of the eight preceding seasonal changes (standardized unexpected earnings on net income).
sign_rationale: Prices underreact to earnings news so firms with high standardized surprises drift upward (post-earnings-announcement drift).
reference: Foster Olsen and Shevlin 1984 (The Accounting Review); Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research); Chan Jegadeesh and Lakonishok 1996 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift; net income replaces EPS before extraordinary items to stay share-basis-free.

economic_definition: Seasonal change in quarterly revenue over the sample standard deviation of the eight preceding seasonal changes (standardized unexpected revenue).
sign_rationale: Revenue surprises carry information beyond earnings surprises and prices drift in their direction.
reference: Jegadeesh and Livnat 2006 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: Seasonal change in quarterly net income over market capitalization (price-scaled earnings surprise).
sign_rationale: Price-deflated seasonal earnings surprises predict post-announcement drift in the surprise direction.
reference: Livnat and Mendenhall 2006 (Journal of Accounting Research); Bernard and Thomas 1989 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Filing-clocked (10-Q plus 46 hours) so the value arrives weeks after the earnings release and misses the announcement return and early drift.

economic_definition: Single-quarter ROE less the same fiscal quarter's ROE a year earlier (dRoe).
sign_rationale: Rising profitability signals higher expected investment returns (q5 expected-growth channel).
reference: Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies); Hou Mo Xue and Zhang 2021 (Review of Finance)

economic_definition: Single-quarter ROA less the same fiscal quarter's ROA a year earlier (dRoa).
sign_rationale: Improving profitability is underreacted fundamental news that predicts higher returns.
reference: Balakrishnan Bartov and Faurel 2010 (Journal of Accounting and Economics); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month SG&A over trailing revenue.
sign_rationale: SG&A builds organization capital that markets may underprice (positive) but is also operating cost that lowers the margins the profitability rows sign positive; pre-registered two-sided.
reference: Eisfeldt and Papanikolaou 2013 (Journal of Finance); Novy-Marx 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics)
admission_note: Eisfeldt and Papanikolaou capitalize SG&A into an organization-capital stock over assets within industries; a flow over sales is a conjecture.

economic_definition: Year-over-year quarterly SG&A growth less year-over-year quarterly revenue growth.
sign_rationale: SG&A growing faster than sales signals cost inefficiency or weakening demand and predicts lower returns.
reference: Lev and Thiagarajan 1993 (Journal of Accounting Research); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year inventory growth less year-over-year quarterly revenue growth.
sign_rationale: Inventory growing faster than sales signals demand weakness or earnings management and predicts lower returns.
reference: Lev and Thiagarajan 1993 (Journal of Accounting Research); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year receivables growth less year-over-year quarterly revenue growth.
sign_rationale: Receivables growing faster than sales signal aggressive revenue recognition or collection problems and predict lower returns.
reference: Lev and Thiagarajan 1993 (Journal of Accounting Research); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Year-over-year quarterly revenue growth less year-over-year quarterly gross-profit growth.
sign_rationale: Gross profit lagging sales signals margin pressure and predicts lower returns.
reference: Lev and Thiagarajan 1993 (Journal of Accounting Research); Abarbanell and Bushee 1998 (The Accounting Review)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month revenue over net operating assets at the start of the trailing year (ATO).
sign_rationale: Efficient use of net operating assets predicts higher future profitability and returns.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Net operating assets net out debt; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in trailing revenue over opening net operating assets.
sign_rationale: Rising asset turnover predicts higher future earnings that prices underreact to.
reference: Soliman 2008 (The Accounting Review)
admission_note: Net operating assets net out debt; debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias (a switch to an unmapped alias has no value) and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total.

economic_definition: Eight-quarter sample standard deviation of single-quarter ROE.
sign_rationale: Volatile profitability is junk; firms with stable ROE earn higher risk-adjusted returns.
reference: Asness Frazzini and Pedersen 2019 (Review of Accounting Studies); Mohanram 2005 (Review of Accounting Studies)
admission_note: Fiscal seasonality in single-quarter ROE inflates the dispersion of seasonal businesses.

economic_definition: Eight-quarter sample standard deviation of single-quarter ROA.
sign_rationale: Stable earnings are more persistent and low earnings variability predicts higher returns.
reference: Mohanram 2005 (Review of Accounting Studies); Dichev and Tang 2009 (Journal of Accounting and Economics)
admission_note: Fiscal seasonality in single-quarter ROA inflates the dispersion of seasonal businesses.

economic_definition: Eight-quarter sample standard deviation of single-quarter operating cash flow over opening total assets.
sign_rationale: Firms with volatile cash flows earn lower returns.
reference: Huang 2009 (Journal of Empirical Finance)
admission_note: Fiscal seasonality in single-quarter operating cash flow inflates the dispersion of seasonal businesses.

economic_definition: Eight-quarter sample standard deviation of year-over-year quarterly revenue growth.
sign_rationale: Volatile sales growth is less predictable and low sales-growth variability predicts higher returns.
reference: Mohanram 2005 (Review of Accounting Studies)

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in net PP&E plus the year-over-year change in inventory over total assets four quarters earlier (I/A).
sign_rationale: Firms that invest more relative to their assets have lower expected returns (q-theory investment effect).
reference: Lyandres Sun and Zhang 2008 (Review of Financial Studies); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: Net PP&E replaces the gross PP&E of Lyandres Sun and Zhang so one PP&E basis spans every issuer and fiscal quarter (gross PP&E is often reported only in the annual note and would jump each fiscal fourth quarter by the year's depreciation); a filer moving to the combined PP&E and finance-lease right-of-use alias at ASC 842 adoption shows a one-time change equal to that asset; an issuer that has never tagged a mapped inventory alias has zero inventory change and otherwise missing inventory has no value.

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in inventory over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Inventory build-ups signal slowing demand and accrual reversal and predict lower returns.
reference: Thomas and Zhang 2002 (Review of Accounting Studies); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)
admission_note: An issuer that has never tagged a mapped inventory alias has zero inventory change; otherwise (a switch to an unmapped alias included) missing inventory has no value.

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month capital expenditure over average total assets.
sign_rationale: High capital investment relative to assets predicts lower returns.
reference: Titman Wei and Xie 2004 (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis); Polk and Sapienza 2009 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Two-year growth of trailing twelve-month capital expenditure.
sign_rationale: Capital-investment growth predicts lower returns as growth options convert into assets in place.
reference: Anderson and Garcia-Feijoo 2006 (Journal of Finance); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Three-year growth of trailing twelve-month capital expenditure.
sign_rationale: Capital-investment growth predicts lower returns as growth options convert into assets in place.
reference: Anderson and Garcia-Feijoo 2006 (Journal of Finance); Hou Xue and Zhang 2020 (Review of Financial Studies)

economic_definition: Trailing twelve-month R&D expense over average total assets.
sign_rationale: R&D-intensive firms earn higher returns because markets underprice intangible investment and its risk.
reference: Li 2011 (Review of Financial Studies); Chan Lakonishok and Sougiannis 2001 (Journal of Finance)

economic_definition: Log change in quarterly weighted-average basic shares over the same fiscal quarter a year earlier (a weighted-share analogue of split-adjusted shares outstanding).
sign_rationale: Firms issue shares when overvalued and repurchase when undervalued so net issuers underperform.
reference: Pontiff and Woodgate 2008 (Journal of Finance); Daniel and Titman 2006 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Fiscal fourth quarters have no value where only annual weighted shares are reported; the two counts are comparable on one filing's restated comparative or daily-bar split epochs (R1d) and labeled incomparable otherwise.

economic_definition: Three-year log change in period-end shares outstanding.
sign_rationale: Sustained net issuance predicts lower returns (composite issuance effect).
reference: Daniel and Titman 2006 (Journal of Finance); Pontiff and Woodgate 2008 (Journal of Finance)
admission_note: Period-end share counts twelve quarters apart are never restated for splits and are comparable only where daily-bar split epochs (R1d) rebase both counts to one split basis and labeled incomparable otherwise.

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in total debt over total assets.
sign_rationale: Rising leverage signals deteriorating financial strength (Piotroski leverage signal).
reference: Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total; a switch to an unmapped alias has no value and never reads as a deleveraging change.

economic_definition: Total debt less cash and short-term investments over common equity (financing leverage).
sign_rationale: Net financial leverage relative to book equity predicts lower returns once operating liability leverage is separated.
reference: Penman Richardson and Tuna 2007 (Journal of Accounting Research)
admission_note: Debt is zero only for an issuer that has never tagged a mapped debt alias and a component missing beside a reported one is absent within the reported total; a switch to an unmapped alias has no value (never a spurious net-cash reading).

economic_definition: Year-over-year change in current assets over current liabilities.
sign_rationale: Improving liquidity is a Piotroski financial-strength signal.
reference: Piotroski 2000 (Journal of Accounting Research)

economic_definition: Trailing cost of revenue plus trailing SG&A over average total assets.
sign_rationale: Firms with high operating costs relative to assets carry operating leverage risk and earn higher returns.
reference: Novy-Marx 2011 (Review of Finance)
admission_note: XBRL SG&A excludes separately reported R&D which the Compustat XSGA of Novy-Marx includes.

economic_definition: Cash and short-term investments over total assets.
sign_rationale: Cash holdings hedge the future investment needs of risky firms and are positively related to expected returns.
reference: Palazzo 2012 (Journal of Financial Economics)
